newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Shell Nigeria says 20 pct of Forcados oil shut in.
newsitem.headline: Shell Nigeria says 20 pct of Forcados oil shut in.

text.p: Royal Dutch/Shell Group's Nigerian unit said on Friday ethnic clashes had forced it to close some Forcados oil output and it had declared force majeure on some cargoes due for lifting from April 29th.
"Some 20 percent of Forcados blend crude has had to be shut in," a Shell spokesman told Reuters in Lagos. "We believe it will affect liftings due from April 29th," he added.
Traders said the reduction was equivalent to about 90,000 barrels per day of production.

Renewed clashes in Nigeria's oil-producing swamps between militant youths of Ijaw and Itsekiri tribes over the relocation of a local council headquarters have claimed many lives and forced Shell to close its Warri flow station last weekend.
The Shell spokesman said, "We have had to close a few fields there," but could not immediately give the exact number.
Early this week, Shell declared force majeure on about 500,000 barrels per day of Bonny crude in Nigeria's southeastern area because of a strike which was called off after two days.
